rules.title: Front stabilizer bushing care

applicability.equipment: Original front stabilizer-bar design; confirm whether the car has the performance package.

rules.what: Check the bushing and its mounting when suspension wear or a knock is investigated. Replace a worn or damaged part after the cause is confirmed.
rules.when: Inspect when a new clunk, loose handling or visible bushing damage appears; replace only when inspection confirms wear or damage.
rules.why: The bushing supports the stabilizer bar while allowing its movement. A knock can also come from links, fasteners or other suspension joints, so the sound alone does not identify this bushing.
notes: Do not apply lubricant to the stabilizer bar or its bushings: it can damage these bushings.
On performance-package vehicles, the front bushings are not replaced separately; the front stabilizer bar is replaced as an assembly.
When separate bushings are fitted, follow the installation orientation and use new bracket bolts. This is repair work, not a periodic greasing task.

rules.title: Rear stabilizer bushing care
rules.what: Inspect the bushing and bracket when rear suspension wear or noise is being investigated. Replace only after the inspection identifies a defect.
rules.when: Inspect when a new rear suspension knock or visible bushing damage appears; replace only when inspection confirms a defect.
rules.why: The bushings locate the bar and isolate its contact with the mounting brackets. Lubrication is not routine care for this design.
notes: Do not lubricate the bar or bushings. Water is permitted on the bracket to help installation; that is not permission to grease the bushing.
Replacement uses new bracket bolts. Rear bushing slits face forward; the front bushing orientation is different.

rules.title: Inspect the suspension rather than replacing it on a timer

matches.titlePattern: ^(?:Suspension System|Front Suspension|Rear Suspension|(?:Front |Rear )?(?:Stabilizer Bar(?: Bushing| Link)?|Lower Arm|Upper Arm|Toe Link|Lower Arm Vertical Link|Shock Absorber|Strut and Spring Assembly|Spring))(?: - .*|)$

rules.what: Inspect suspension parts and fasteners for wear, damage or looseness; investigate a new knock, pull or ride-height change rather than assuming one part is responsible.
rules.when: At each oil-change service; investigate a new symptom sooner.
rules.why: Suspension parts hold the wheel in position as loads change. Wear can affect tire contact and alignment before a part completely fails.
notes: This inspection interval does not create a scheduled replacement age for bushings, arms, springs or dampers.
Lubricate only actual grease fittings where fitted; do not apply that instruction to rubber bushings.

rules.title: Wheel and hub condition

matches.titlePattern: ^(?:(?:Front )?Wheel Bearing and Wheel Hub|Wheel and Tire|Wheels and Tires)(?: - .*|)$

rules.what: Check for wheel-related noise, wear, looseness or drag. A confirmed fault needs diagnosis of the bearing, tire, brake and mounting as appropriate.
rules.when: At each oil-change service; check an unusual noise or looseness sooner.
rules.why: A sound that follows road speed is a clue, not proof that the wheel bearing needs replacement.

rules.title: Tire pressure and tread

matches.titlePattern: ^(?:Wheel and Tire|Wheels and Tires|Tire Pressure Monitoring System \(TPMS\)(?: - Overview| - System Operation and Component Description)?|Tire Pressure Monitoring System \(TPMS\) Sensor)$

rules.what: Check tire pressure and inspect wear, including the spare if fitted. Use the vehicle label for the correct cold pressure.
rules.when: Monthly; also inspect tread at each oil-change service.
rules.why: Pressure supports the load and affects the tire’s contact with the road. A pressure-monitoring system does not replace a physical tire inspection.
notes: Follow the rotation pattern for the actual tire sizes and directional markings; do not assume front and rear wheels are interchangeable.

rules.title: Brake wear and hose condition

matches.titlePattern: ^(?:Brake System|Front Disc Brake|Rear Disc Brake|Brake Pads|Brake Disc|Brake Caliper|(?:Front|Rear) Brake Flexible Hose)(?: - .*|)$

rules.what: Inspect pads, discs and brake hoses. Replacement depends on measured wear or a diagnosed defect, not a universal mileage.
rules.when: At every oil-change service. A change in braking performance needs attention before the next service.
rules.why: Pads wear as they turn motion into heat. Hose damage, uneven wear and disc condition need separate checks; new pads alone do not address every braking concern.
notes: Use the limits and procedure for the fitted brake package; 2-, 4- and 6-piston front systems are not interchangeable specifications.

rules.title: Parking-brake operation

matches.titlePattern: ^(?:Parking Brake|Parking Brake Cable Adjustment|Parking Brake Cable (?:LH|RH)|Parking Brake Control)$

rules.what: Check that the parking brake applies and releases correctly. Adjustment or replacement follows an identified problem.
rules.when: Every six months, and during oil-change brake inspections.
rules.why: The parking brake must both hold when applied and release so the rear brakes do not drag.

rules.title: Steering linkage and joint condition

matches.titlePattern: ^(?:Tie Rod|Tie Rod End|Steering Gear|Power Steering(?: - Overview| - System Operation and Component Description)?)$

rules.what: Inspect steering linkage and joints for wear, damage or looseness.
rules.when: At each oil-change service; investigate a change in steering feel or noise sooner.
rules.why: The tie rods carry steering movement from the rack to the wheels. Joint wear can let wheel direction change without the intended steering input.

rules.title: Electric steering needs no fluid top-up

matches.titlePattern: ^(?:Steering Gear|Power Steering(?: - Overview| - System Operation and Component Description)?)$

rules.what: There is no hydraulic power-steering reservoir to top up or power-steering fluid to flush.
rules.when: No power-steering fluid service interval.
rules.why: Electric assistance comes from a motor, so a hydraulic-fluid maintenance routine does not apply.

rules.title: Engine oil and filter

matches.titlePattern: ^(?:Engine(?: - Overview| Component View)?|Oil Pan|Oil Pump|Oil Filter Inspection|Engine Oil Draining and Filling)$

rules.what: Change the engine oil and filter, then reset the oil-life monitor. Check the oil level between services.
rules.when: Follow the oil-life message; never exceed 1 year or 10,000 mi (16,000 km). Check the level monthly.
rules.why: Oil lubricates moving parts and carries contaminants to the filter. Oil life and oil quantity are different checks: the monitor does not replace checking the level.
notes: Complete a requested oil change within 2 weeks or 500 mi (800 km). If the monitor is inoperative or reset too soon, use 6 months or 5,000 mi (8,000 km) from the last change.
For predominantly dusty or sandy driving, use 5,000 mi (8,000 km) or 6 months. Other severe-use and hot-climate rules can differ; use the linked operating-conditions schedule.
Use the oil grade and specification for the selected engine. Track-use and 5.2L schedules are not supplied by this item.

rules.title: Engine air-filter element

matches.titlePattern: ^(?:Air Cleaner|Intake Air Distribution and Filtering)$

rules.what: Replace the engine air-filter element. Keep the element seated correctly in its housing.
rules.when: Every 30,000 mi (48,000 km) in normal use.
rules.why: The element traps airborne dirt before it reaches the engine. Replacing the filter element does not mean replacing the entire air-cleaner housing.
notes: Predominantly dusty or sandy use calls for inspection at 15,000 mi (24,000 km) and replacement as needed. Dirty conditions can shorten filter life.

rules.title: Cabin air filter
rules.what: Replace the cabin filter; it cleans air entering the heating and air-conditioning system.
rules.when: Every 20,000 mi (32,000 km) in normal use.
rules.why: A loaded filter restricts cabin airflow. It is a different service item from the engine air filter.
notes: Inspect more often and replace as needed with sustained dusty conditions or extensive low-speed commercial use.

rules.title: Spark plugs

matches.titlePattern: ^Spark Plugs$

rules.what: Replace the spark plugs with the specified type for this engine.
rules.when: Every 100,000 mi (160,000 km) in normal use.
rules.why: The electrodes wear as sparks repeatedly jump the gap. A scheduled plug change is distinct from diagnosing a misfire.
notes: Ford specifies 60,000 mi (96,000 km) for predominantly towing/car-top-carrier use or extensive idling/low-speed commercial use.
A misfire can have ignition, fuel or mechanical causes; it does not automatically mean the plug or coil has failed.

rules.title: Engine coolant service

matches.titlePattern: ^Engine Cooling(?: - Component Location| - System Operation and Component Description| System Draining, Vacuum Filling and Bleeding| System Flushing)?$

rules.what: Replace the coolant using the specified fluid and the correct filling and bleeding procedure.
rules.when: First at 6 years or 100,000 mi (160,000 km); then every 3 years or 50,000 mi (80,000 km), whichever comes first.
rules.why: Coolant carries heat and protects internal surfaces. Correct concentration and removal of trapped air matter as well as the amount added.
notes: This is a coolant interval, not a scheduled replacement interval for the radiator, thermostat or coolant pump.

rules.title: Cooling-system condition

matches.titlePattern: ^(?:Engine Cooling(?: - Component Location| - System Operation and Component Description)?|Coolant Pump|Radiator|Degas Bottle|Thermostat(?: Housing)?|Cooling Fan Motor and Shroud)$

rules.what: Inspect coolant strength and hoses during service; check coolant level and strength between services. Investigate leakage or overheating rather than repeatedly topping up.
rules.when: At oil-change service; check level and strength every six months.
rules.why: A leak or deteriorated hose can reduce cooling even when the pump and radiator still work. The check is for the system’s condition, not an automatic shopping list.
notes: Let the cooling system cool before opening its pressure cap. Use the engine-specific procedure for filling or repairs.

rules.title: Accessory belts

matches.titlePattern: ^(?:Accessory Drive(?: - Component Location)?|Accessory Drive Belt|Air Conditioning \(A/C\) Compressor Belt)$

rules.what: Inspect the accessory belts and replace them at the scheduled interval or earlier if their condition requires it.
rules.when: Inspect at 100,000 mi (160,000 km), then every other oil change until replacement. Replace at 150,000 mi (240,000 km).
rules.why: The belt carries mechanical power to its driven accessories. Age and wear affect the belt even when its pulleys are still serviceable.
notes: The replacement interval belongs to the belts; it does not automatically require new tensioners or pulleys.

rules.title: Belt and pulley condition
rules.what: Check for belt contamination, missing rib material, misalignment and pulley damage when noise or visible deterioration appears.
rules.when: When a concern appears, and during belt service; no separate timed tensioner or pulley replacement is assigned.
rules.why: A noise may come from incorrect belt seating, a contaminated belt, a pulley or an accessory. Identifying the cause prevents replacing a good tensioner while the real problem remains.
notes: Do not lubricate the belt. Small cracks alone are not a failure: exposed cord or missing chunks are unacceptable conditions.

rules.title: 6R80 automatic transmission fluid and filter

matches.titlePattern: ^(?:Transmission(?: - .*| Description(?: - Overview| - System Operation and Component Description)?)?|Transmission Fluid (?:Drain and Refill|Exchange|Level Check|Pan, Gasket and Filter))$

rules.what: Change the automatic-transmission fluid and filter using the 6R80 procedure and specified fluid.
rules.when: Every 150,000 mi (240,000 km) in normal use.
rules.why: The fluid is both a lubricant and a hydraulic working fluid. Correct level and temperature-controlled checking matter; the amount drained is not a universal refill capacity.
notes: Do not apply this automatic-transmission interval or fluid specification to an MT82 or 3160 manual gearbox.

rules.title: MT82 manual transmission fluid

matches.titlePattern: ^(?:Manual Transmission(?: - Component Location| - Overview| - System Operation and Component Description)?|Transmission(?: - .*| Draining and Filling| Fluid Level Check)?)$

rules.what: Change the manual-transmission fluid using the MT82 procedure and its specified lubricant.
rules.when: Every 150,000 mi (240,000 km) in normal use.
rules.why: The lubricant protects gears and bearings and must suit the transmission’s synchronizers. Manual and automatic transmission fluids are not interchangeable choices.
notes: For predominantly towing/car-top-carrier use: 60,000 mi (96,000 km). For predominantly dusty or sandy driving: 50,000 mi (80,000 km).
This MT82 guidance does not establish a 5.2L/3160 service interval.

rules.title: Driveshaft and joint inspection

matches.titlePattern: ^Driveshaft(?: Universal Joint| Angle Measurement| Runout and Balancing)?$

rules.what: Inspect the driveshaft and joints. Investigate vibration, wear or looseness; lubricate only if the fitted joint has a grease fitting.
rules.when: At each oil-change service; inspect more frequently with predominantly towing/car-top-carrier use.
rules.why: The shaft carries torque while the joints accommodate movement. A vibration does not by itself identify which joint or shaft part is responsible.

rules.title: Halfshaft dust boots

matches.titlePattern: ^Rear (?:Drive Halfshafts|Halfshaft)$

rules.what: Inspect the halfshaft boots for damage and escaping grease. A split boot needs assessment before contamination harms the joint.
rules.when: At each oil-change service; check a visible grease leak sooner.
rules.why: The flexible boot keeps joint grease in and road contamination out. Boot damage and complete joint failure are different findings.

rules.title: Rear axle leakage or water exposure

matches.titlePattern: ^(?:Rear Drive Axle and Differential(?: - Overview)?|Axle Assembly|Axle and Differential Draining and Filling|Differential Fluid Level Check|Differential Housing Cover|Drive Pinion Seal|Rear Halfshaft Seal)$

rules.what: Have a suspected axle leak or an axle that has been submerged in water checked promptly.
rules.when: As soon as leakage or submersion is suspected.
rules.why: A low level or water contamination can compromise lubrication. A wet seal, flood exposure and a routine time-based service are different reasons to inspect the axle.
notes: The linked Ford normal schedule lists a 150,000 mi axle-fluid change, while its axle exception says checks or changes are not required unless leakage or submersion is suspected. Confirm the applicable instruction for the vehicle before assigning a routine fluid-change date.

rules.title: Battery terminal connections

matches.titlePattern: ^(?:Battery|Battery Cables(?: - .*)?|Battery and Cables - (?:Overview|System Operation and Component Description)|Battery Disconnect and Connect|Battery Charging)$

rules.what: Check battery connections and clean them if needed. Use the battery disconnect/connect procedure when work requires disconnection.
rules.when: Every six months.
rules.why: A poor connection can interrupt the high current needed for starting even when the battery itself is serviceable.
notes: A weak-start concern needs a battery and connection assessment.

rules.title: Washer fluid and spray

matches.titlePattern: ^(?:Windshield Washer (?:Pump|Reservoir)|Washer Hose (?:Repair|Coupling)|Wipers and Washers(?: - Overview| - System Operation and Component Description)?)$

rules.what: Check washer-fluid level and confirm that the spray reaches the glass.
rules.when: Fluid level monthly; spray and wiper operation every six months.
rules.why: A working pump is useful only if fluid can reach the windshield. Low fluid and a spray problem are different checks.

rules.title: Wiper operation and blade condition

matches.titlePattern: ^(?:Windshield Wiper (?:Motor|Pivot Arm)|Wiper Linkage Assembly|Wipers and Washers(?: - Overview| - System Operation and Component Description)?)$

rules.what: Check wiping performance; clean or replace the blades as their condition requires.
rules.when: Every six months and when wiping becomes ineffective.
rules.why: Blades are wear items. Streaking can be a blade or glass-cleanliness issue; it does not automatically call for a new motor or linkage.

rules.title: Exhaust and heat-shield condition

matches.titlePattern: ^(?:Exhaust System|Catalytic Converter(?: - .*)?|Muffler and Tailpipe|Muffler|Exhaust Intermediate Pipe)$

rules.what: Inspect the exhaust system and heat shields for condition and secure mounting.
rules.when: At each oil-change service.
rules.why: The exhaust carries hot gases away, while its shields protect nearby areas from heat. A loose shield and an exhaust leak need different repairs.

rules.title: Exterior light operation

matches.titlePattern: ^(?:Exterior Lighting - (?:Overview|System Operation and Component Description)|Headlamp (?:Assembly|Bulb)|Headlamps|Rear Lamp Assembly|Fog Lamp(?: Bulb| Assembly)?|License Plate Lamp)$

rules.what: Check that the exterior lamps operate correctly. Diagnose an inoperative lamp before assuming its bulb is the only cause.
rules.when: Monthly.
rules.why: The checks cover both seeing the road and being visible to other drivers; an electrical fault can affect a good lamp.

rules.title: Hinges, latches and external locks

matches.titlePattern: ^(?:Door Latch Lubrication|Front Door Latch|Hood Latch|Luggage Compartment Lid Latch - (?:Coupe|Convertible)|Handles, Locks, Latches and Entry Systems - (?:Overview|System Operation and Component Description)|Locks, Latches and Entry Systems)$

rules.what: Check operation and lubricate only where the relevant component procedure calls for it.
rules.when: Every six months; address sticking or failure to latch sooner.
rules.why: A latch must engage and release reliably. The correct lubricant and application point depend on the mechanism.

rules.title: Seatbelt wear and function

matches.titlePattern: ^(?:(?:Front|Rear) Seatbelt (?:Buckle|Retractor(?: and Pretensioner)?)(?: - Coupe| - Convertible)?|Seatbelt Maintenance|Seatbelt Cleaning|Seatbelt Systems(?: - System Operation and Component Description)?)$

rules.what: Inspect the belt’s condition and check that its buckle and retractor work correctly.
rules.when: Every six months; collision-related inspection is a separate requirement.
rules.why: The webbing, latch and retractor must work together to restrain an occupant. A normal visual check does not establish that a collision-loaded assembly is reusable.
notes: Use the dedicated restraint procedure for any repair; this check is not an instruction to probe a pretensioner circuit.
